source_text: Καὶ ἡ τῆς σεμιδάλεως δὲ προσφορά, ὦ ἄνδρες, ἔλεγον, ἡ ὑπὲρ τῶν καθαριζομένων ἀπὸ τῆς λέπρας προσφέρεσθαι παραδοθεῖσα . τύπος ἦν τοῦ ἄρτου τῆς εὐχαριστίας, ὃν εἰς ἀνάμνησιν τοῦ πάθους, οὗ ἔπαθεν ὑπὲρ τῶν καθαιρομένων τὰς ψυχὰς ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας ἀνθρώπων, Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν παρέδωκε ποιεῖν , ἵνα ἅμα τε εὐχαριστῶμεν τῷ θεῷ ὑπέρ τε τοῦ τὸν κόσμον ἐκτικέναι σὺν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐν αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς κακίας, ἐν ᾖ γεγόναμεν, ἠλευθερωκέναι ἡμᾶς, καὶ τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας καταλελυκέναι τελείαν κατάλυσιν διὰ τοῦ παθητοῦ γενομένου κατὰ τὴν βουλὴν αὐτοῦ. Ὅθεν περὶ μὲν τῶν ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν τότε προσφερομένων θυσιῶν λέγει ὁ θεός, ὡς προέφην, διὰ Μαλαχίου, ἑνὸς τῶν δώδεκα· Οὐκ ἔστι θέλημά μου ἐν ὑμῖν, λέγει κύριος, καὶ τὰς θυσίας ὑμῶν οὐ προσδέξομαι ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν ὑμῶν· διότι ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου ἕως δυσμῶν τὸ ὄνομά μου δεδόξασται ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι, καὶ ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ θυμίαμα προσφέρεται τῷ ὀνόματί μου καὶ θυσία καθαρά, ὅτι μέγα τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι, λέγει κύριος, ὑμεῖς δὲ βεβηλοῦτε αὐτό . Περὶ δὲ τῶν ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν τῶν ἐθνῶν προσφερομένων αὐτῷ θυσιῶν, τουτέστι τοῦ ἄρτου τῆς εὐχαριστίας καὶ τοῦ ποτηρίου ὁμοίως τῆς εὐχαριστίας, προλέγει τότε, εἰπὼν καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ δοξάζειν ἡμᾶς, ὑμᾶς δὲ βεβηλοῦν. Ἡ δὲ ἐντολὴ τῆς περιτομῆς, κελεύουσα τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκ παντὸς περιτέμνειν τὰ γεννώμενα , τύπος ἦν τῆς ἀληθινῆς περιτομῆς, ἣν περιετμήθημεν ἀπὸ τῆς πλάνης καὶ πονηρίας διὰ τοῦ ἀπὸ νεκρῶν ἀναστάντος τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ἡμέρᾳ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν· μία γὰρ τῶν σαββάτων, πρώτη μὲν οὖσα τῶν πασῶν ἡμερῶν, κατὰ τὸν ἀριθμὸν πάλιν τῶν πασῶν ἡμερῶν τῆς κυκλοφορίας ὀγδόη καλεῖται, καὶ πρώτη οὖσα μένει.
thought_title: The Offering of Fine Flour and Circumcision
pass_a_gloss: And the offering of fine flour, men, was said to be given on behalf of those being cleansed from leprosy. It was a type of the bread of the Eucharist, which Jesus Christ our Lord gave to do in remembrance of the passion, which He suffered on behalf of those being cleansed of their souls from all wickedness of men, so that at the same time we give thanks to God for the world which He has begotten with all things in it through man, and for freeing us from the evil in which we were, and for destroying the rulers and authorities through the passion that occurred according to His will. Wherefore God says concerning the sacrifices that were being offered by you at that time, as I said before, through Malachi, one of the twelve: 'It is not my will in you,' says the Lord, 'and I will not accept your sacrifices from your hands; for from the rising of the sun to the setting, my name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name and a pure sacrifice, for my name is great among the nations,' says the Lord, 'but you profane it.' And concerning the sacrifices that are being offered to Him by us Gentiles in every place, that is, the bread of the Eucharist and the cup of the Eucharist similarly, He spoke beforehand, saying that we glorify His name, but you profane it. And the commandment of circumcision, which commands to circumcise on the eighth day all that are born, was a type of the true circumcision, which we have been circumcised with, from deception and wickedness, through Jesus Christ our Lord, who rose from the dead on the first day of the week; for the first day of the week, being one of all the days, is called the eighth according to the number of all the days of the cycle, and being first, it remains.

pass_b_english: The offering of fine flour, gentlemen, was said to be presented on behalf of those being cleansed from leprosy. It served as a type of the bread of the Eucharist, which Jesus Christ our Lord commanded us to perform in remembrance of the passion he endured on behalf of those being cleansed in their souls from all human wickedness, so that we might at once give thanks to God for having brought the world into being with all that it contains for the sake of humanity, for having freed us from the evil in which we were ensnared, and for having brought the rulers and authorities to nothing through the suffering that came to pass according to his will.

Therefore, concerning the sacrifices you were offering at that time, God says — as I mentioned before — through Malachi, one of the twelve: "I have no pleasure in you," says the Lord, "and I will not accept your sacrifices from your hands. For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name and a pure sacrifice, for my name is great among the nations," says the Lord, "but you profane it" (Malachi 1:10-11). And concerning the sacrifices we Gentiles now offer to him in every place — that is, the bread of the Eucharist and likewise the cup of the Eucharist — he spoke beforehand, declaring that we glorify his name while you profane it.

The commandment of circumcision, which orders that every male be circumcised on the eighth day, was a type of the true circumcision by which we have been circumcised from deception and wickedness through Jesus Christ our Lord, who rose from the dead on the first day of the week. For the first day of the week, though it is the first of all days, is also called the eighth according to the reckoning of all the days of the cycle, and it remains the first.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the theological nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between the 'type' (τύπος) and the reality, the causal relationship of the passion to the cleansing of souls, and the complex explanation of the 'eighth day' as the first day of the week. Scripture citations (Malachi 1:10-11) are correctly added to the English text to identify the quoted Malachi passage.
